To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PLGA microsphere construct with heparin/pLLy nanoparticles loaded with TGF-beta3 is useful in the neocartilage engineering.
we have fabricated nanostructured 3-dimensional (3D) scaffolds for growth factor release using poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)-based microspheres.

we have devised a method for the fabrication 3D scaffolding system of nanostructure that growth factor loaded nanoparticles were attached on the positively charge surface of PLGA microparticles precoated with low-molecular weight of poly(ethylenimine) via LbL system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a PLGA-based microsphere construct coated by growth factor loaded nanoparticles.
a novel method for fabricating 3D scaffolding for tissue engineering applications using a layer-by-layer assembly method.
the fabrication of PLGA microspere construct coated with heparin/pL-lysine loaded nanoparticles as a novel cell supporting matrix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this PLGA microsphere system can be a useful scaffold to control growth factor delivery and to promote neocartilage regeneration.

the TGF-beta 2 and 3 loaded heparin/P(Lys) nanoparticles were effectively immobilized onto the PLGA microsphere surface and the TGF-beta loaded nanoparticles were released in a prolonged manner in vitro.
the PLGA microsphere construct containing TGF-beta loaded heparin/PL nanoparticles can be applied as an effective scaffold for neocartilaginous matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PLGA microsphere construct containing growth factor loaded nanoparticles can be used to promote neocartilage regeneration.
PLGA microsphere construct can be applied as a cell supportive matrix to induce the neocartilage regeneration.

PLGA microsphere construct can provide a 3D scaffold to support cell attachment and proliferation, and growth factor loaded hepanin/poly(L-Lysine) nanoparticle can be used to control growth factor release and cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PLGA micropheres as a cell carrier can provide a novel method for stem cell delivery.
the LbL method can be used to create 3D nanostructured scaffolds that can be used as a novel cell supporting matrix.
we can fabricate nanostructured 3-dimensional scaffolds by the LbL technique and the nanostructured PLGA microspherematrix could be a useful tool in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
